title: every job carries a Node 20 deprecation warning, and a push that moves only a board spends a full CI run
body:
## What happens

Every job of every run carries a deprecation annotation: `actions/checkout@v4` targets Node 20, and GitHub is already forcing those actions onto Node 24. It is a warning today and an expiry later, and it is on every job because `actions/checkout` is the only action either of devbin's workflows uses (vc scanned 24 workflow files across 18 estates; devbin's half is `tests.yml` and `release.yml`).

Separately, a push to `main` starts a run whatever it changed. A large share of devbin's pushes move only the whiteboard's generated boards under `intent/whiteboard/`, which no job reads, so a full Ubuntu run is spent proving that a board file did not break the shell.

**Measured by vc on 2026-09-22, board-only commits over the previous 30 days**: devbin 427 of 898, which is 47%. Across the fleet: Laksa 56%, Intent 48%, Lamplight 46%, Gtools 39%, Conflab 33%, Utilz 33%, Prolix 33%, Baize 24%, Cdtempl 16%, Molt 4%, and arca_cli, arca_config and Riffle none at all.

**Two limits on that figure, stated because the number otherwise reads wider than the measurement.** It counts COMMITS, and CI runs on PUSHES: a push carrying one board-only commit and one code commit still starts a run, so the real saving is lower than this share and cannot be derived from this data. And an earlier cut of the same query counted commits TOUCHING the whiteboard rather than confined to it, which gave devbin 62% -- an upper bound that would have overstated the case by a third.

## Ruling

hv, 2026-09-22, on the fleet CI pass: "Minimise warnings, aim for pristine whenever we can". That takes in every action still running on Node 20, `paths-ignore` for `intent/whiteboard/**`, and devbin's own workflows as well as the estates'.

## Fix

**`actions/checkout@v4` becomes `@v7` in both workflows.** v7.0.1 (2026-07-20) is the latest release and runs on `node24`, read from `action.yml` at that ref rather than from memory. The two majors in between change one thing each that could matter and neither reaches these workflows: v6 persists credentials to a separate file, and v7 refuses to check out a fork's pull request under `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`. Neither event appears in any workflow in any estate (vc's scan). The version is hv's latest-deps ruling; the FLOOR, which is what a test can hold, is v5, the first major on Node 24.

**`on.push` gains `paths-ignore` for `intent/whiteboard/**`**, so a push that only moves a board starts no run.

**A path filter cannot suppress the tag trigger 0108 added.** GitHub's workflow syntax reference says path filters are not evaluated for pushes of tags, and that where both `branches` and `paths-ignore` are given, both must be satisfied. This deserves a sentence in the file itself: the line reads as though it should also filter tags, and the only thing saying otherwise is a sentence of documentation, so the next reader is one plausible inference away from "fixing" a correct file.

## Consequences to state in the docs

A board-only push now has no run of its own, which is the point. "CI is green on the pushed commit" therefore reads on the last run there was -- the last pushed commit that changed anything CI covers. That sits beside 0108's consequence, where a superseded run is cancelled, and the two together mean a pushed sha having no verdict is ordinary rather than a signal.

## Tests

`tests/unit/ci-workflow.bats`:

- Every `uses:` of `actions/checkout` in both workflows is at or above the Node 24 floor. **The arm holds the FLOOR and not the adopted version, because the floor is the property under test**: what matters is that an action runs on Node 24, and v5 is the first major that does, read from each ref's own `action.yml`. Which major we pin is an incidental of the latest-deps ruling, so a later bump to v8 needs no test edit, while the drift arm below still catches a bump that reached one file and not the other. (An earlier draft of this justified the same decision by saying that an arm pinning the newest would redden the day GitHub shipped the next major. It would not: nothing in this repository changes when they ship, so such an arm reddens only on an edit here. Right decision, false reason, which is the pairing that reads as settled -- vc caught it.)
- Both workflows agree on that version, so the two files cannot drift apart unnoticed.
- `on.push` carries `paths-ignore` for the whiteboard AND still carries the tag filter, asserted together, because the risk is one being removed in the belief that it cancels the other.

Red first for each, and the floor arm is driven with a v4 to prove it can fail.

## Resolution

Fixed at `993c995`, alongside 0108 in one commit: both edit `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, and splitting them would have meant hunk surgery on one file rather than two honest changes.

`actions/checkout` moves from v4 to v7 in both workflows, four uses. Verified at the source rather than from release notes: v4 declares `using: node20`, and v5, v6 and v7 all declare `node24`. No workflow in the fleet uses `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`, checked across all 24 workflow files in 18 repositories, so v7's fork-PR change cannot reach any of them.

`on.push` ignores paths under `intent/whiteboard/**`. Measured: 427 of devbin's last 898 commits, 47%, changed nothing outside `intent/whiteboard/`. Two limits on that figure, stated because the claim would otherwise read wider than the measurement: CI runs on PUSHES rather than commits, so a push carrying one board commit and one code commit still runs; and a first cut of this counted commits TOUCHING the whiteboard, which gave 62% and would have overstated it by a third.

The arms hold the floor rather than the adopted version: v5 is the first major on Node 24, which is the PROPERTY that matters, so a later bump to v8 needs no test edit while a drift arm still catches a half-done bump. The comment carrying that reasoning first said an arm pinning the newest "would go red the day GitHub ships the next one", which is false -- it reddens only when somebody edits the file -- and the correction is recorded in place, because the next reader of that arm is whoever does the v8 bump.

Verified by GitHub's own documentation: path filters are not evaluated for pushes of tags, so this cannot suppress the release run 0108 depends on, and the arm asserting the filter asserts the tag trigger in the same breath, because the hazard is a reader deleting one in the belief that it affects the other.

Full suite 1600/1600 at `993c995`, 0 not ok. Ships in 0.1.6.
